questions.question: You’re waiting in line at the café, and the person in front of you drops their bag. What is the most appropriate response if you want to help without being too direct?
options: ‘I’m so sorry, but I can’t help with that right now.’
‘Here, let me take a look—maybe it’s just lost.’
‘Oh dear, that’s a shame! You should get someone else to help.’
‘I’m afraid I don’t know what happened. You’ll have to ask someone else.’
questions.answer: ‘Here, let me take a look—maybe it’s just lost.’

questions.question: Your colleague says, ‘I think we should move the meeting to the afternoon.’ What is the best way to politely agree but suggest an alternative time?
options: ‘That’s a great idea! I’ll make sure to book it for 2 PM.’
‘I’m not sure about that—maybe we should keep it at 10 AM?’
‘Yes, that sounds fine. I’ll just check my diary.’
‘I don’t think that’s a good time for everyone.’
questions.answer: ‘That’s a great idea! I’ll make sure to book it for 2 PM.’

questions.question: A friend says, ‘I really wish I could come to your party tomorrow, but I have a prior commitment.’ What is the most appropriate way to respond if you want to politely offer them an alternative?
options: ‘Oh, that’s too bad. Maybe next weekend?’
‘I’m sorry to hear that—you should definitely come another time.’
‘No, that’s fine—I’ll see you tomorrow anyway.’
‘I don’t think you should make any plans for now.’
questions.answer: ‘Oh, that’s too bad. Maybe next weekend?’

questions.question: During a formal presentation, a participant interrupts you and says, ‘Actually, I think we should reconsider this approach.’ What is the best way to respond if you want to acknowledge their opinion but maintain your position?
options: ‘That’s an interesting point. Let’s discuss it further in the break.’
‘I disagree completely—this is the best solution.’
‘You’re right; we should definitely change it.’
‘I’m not sure why you’re bringing that up.’
questions.answer: ‘That’s an interesting point. Let’s discuss it further in the break.’

questions.question: Your boss asks, ‘Do you have any questions before we start the project?’ You want to politely express your concern about the tight deadline. What is the best way to respond?
options: ‘I’m afraid I don’t have any questions at the moment.’
‘I’m a bit worried about the deadline—could we discuss it later?’
‘I think we should ignore this concern and move forward.’
‘This seems like a bad idea—let’s cancel the project.’
questions.answer: ‘I’m a bit worried about the deadline—could we discuss it later?’
